edges.description: The knockout reproduces the cardinal cardiac phenotype of the human disease at both the functional and histological level, which is what makes it usable as the tissue-level evidence for a node that has never been biopsied in a patient.
edges.limitations: A complete knockout in a fish, against biallelic missense and truncating alleles in humans, several of which retain partial activity. The cardiac readout is embryonic and the human cardiomyopathy is progressive over years. Nothing here models the encephalopathy or the thalamic lesions, which are the features that distinguish this disease from MTO1 deficiency. And one of the model's own findings - globally increased tRNA aminoacylation - has no reported human counterpart.

edges.description: The surviving knock-in genotypes develop cardiac and muscular dysfunction that the authors attribute to altered mitochondrial translation, which is the same causal step the human entry asserts.
edges.limitations: A mouse, and one reported in a single 2026 paper with no independent replication. The lethal genotype cannot be studied postnatally at all, so the model covers the milder half of the allelic range by construction. The mouse phenotype is described as cardiac and muscular; no thalamic or encephalopathic phenotype is reported, so the neurological half of the human disease remains unmodelled in any mammal.

edges.description: Virus-mediated expression of Gtpbp3 reversed the mitochondrial dysfunction and pathology in these animals as well as in cells, which is the first intervention result reported for this disease.
edges.limitations: Preclinical. This is a mouse rescue in a single study; no human trial exists and none is registered. The report does not establish durability, dose, delivery route in humans, or whether the neurological phenotype - absent from the mouse - would respond at all. Reading it as a therapy in prospect for patients would go beyond what the source claims.

nodes.description: Two damaged copies of GTPBP3. The allelic spectrum is broad - missense, frameshift, in-frame deletion, nonsense and splice-site changes are all reported - and the mechanism is loss of function. Two quantitative observations give that reading its force: loss-of-function variants are markedly over-represented in patients relative to gnomAD, and patient variants cluster significantly in the TrmE-type G domain that binds guanine nucleotides and Mg2+ and hydrolyses GTP. The recurrent c.689A>C (p.Gln230Pro) allele is a hotspot, particularly in Chinese cohorts.

nodes.description: Cardiac muscle has among the highest oxidative demands in the body, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the feature this disease was named for. What the human data establish is the association; the causal step from a translation defect to myocyte hypertrophy is supplied by the zebrafish knockout, in which loss of gtpbp3 produced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and myocardial fibre disarray in the ventricles together with reduced fractional shortening, and by knock-in mice carrying patient alleles, which develop cardiac and muscular dysfunction attributed to altered mitochondrial translation.

nodes.description: The biochemical endpoint the entity is named for, and it is variable rather than stereotyped. Eight of the nine founding families showed combined respiratory chain complex deficiencies in skeletal muscle; ClinGen describes the muscle findings across the literature as variable. In the Italian sibship complex IV was reduced by 61 percent in muscle with complex I at the lower limit of control, and ATP synthesis in fibroblast mitochondria was reduced by 38 to 49 percent depending on substrate. Variability of which complexes are hit is expected from the mechanism: a translation defect degrades all four mtDNA-dependent complexes, and which one falls furthest in a given assay is a matter of tissue and threshold rather than of a distinct lesion.

nodes.description: The one thing that separates this disease from MTO1 deficiency at the cellular level. Both enzymes catalyse the same modification and both defects cause infantile hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with lactic acidosis, but the compensatory response runs in opposite directions. MTO1-deficient fibroblasts inactivate AMPK, down-regulate UCP2 and PPAR-gamma and activate HIF-1; GTPBP3-depleted cells do the reverse - AMPK is activated, UCP2 and PPAR-gamma rise and HIF-1 is inactivated. The authors read that divergence as evidence that one of the two proteins has a role beyond tRNA modification.

evidence.reference_title: Defects in the mitochondrial-tRNA modification enzymes MTO1 and GTPBP3 promote different metabolic reprogramming through a HIF-PPARγ-UCP2-AMPK axis.
evidence.snippet: Unexpectedly, this response is different from that triggered by the GTPBP3 defect, as GTPBP3-depleted cells exhibit AMPK activation, increased levels of UCP2 and PPARγ, and inactivation of HIF-1.

evidence.reference_title: Defects in the mitochondrial-tRNA modification enzymes MTO1 and GTPBP3 promote different metabolic reprogramming through a HIF-PPARγ-UCP2-AMPK axis.
evidence.snippet: Therefore, the HIF-PPARγ-UCP2-AMPK axis is operating differently in MTO1- and GTPBP3-defective cells, which strongly suggests that one of these proteins has an additional role, besides mitochondrial-tRNA modification.

nodes.description: Wobble hypomodification degrades codon-anticodon pairing, so synthesis of the thirteen mtDNA-encoded respiratory chain subunits falls. The founding series calls this a severe mitochondrial translation defect. Because those thirteen subunits are distributed across complexes I, III, IV and V, the downstream deficiency is combined rather than isolated - which is the structural reason this disease is named as a combined oxidative phosphorylation defect.

nodes.description: GTPBP3 and MTO1 jointly catalyse the formation of 5-taurinomethyluridine at the wobble (position 34) uridine of five mitochondrial tRNAs - those for Gln, Glu, Lys, Leu(UUR) and Trp. GTPBP3 contributes the potassium-dependent GTPase activity and binds methylene-tetrahydrofolate; the modification promotes decoding at cognate codons and restricts mispairing at near-cognate ones. Patient alleles reduce or abolish that activity, and structural work on individual variants shows multimerisation, aggregation and proteasomal degradation of the protein as the route to it.

nodes.description: A CRISPR/Cas9 gtpbp3 knockout in zebrafish, and the model that supplies the tissue-level account this disease otherwise lacks. Loss of gtpbp3 altered tRNA folding and, unexpectedly, globally increased mitochondrial tRNA aminoacylation efficiency; it impaired mitochondrial translation, produced proteostasis stress and altered respiratory chain complex activities. The animals developed abnormal embryonic heart development with reduced ventricular fractional shortening, cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and myocardial fibre disarray.
